result.title: Corpus Explorer — React web workbench over the chunk database

facts.text: `notebooklm-server` serves the built React app at `/ui`; opening it in a browser loads the Corpus Explorer.
Every new corpus endpoint lives under `/v1/corpus/*` and returns 401 without the `NOTEBOOKLM_SERVER_TOKEN` bearer token.
The UI asks for the server token once and stays signed in across page reloads.
When Postgres is unreachable, corpus routes return 503 and the UI shows a blocking 'database unreachable' screen — never an empty corpus.
Frontend source lives in `web/` (Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + TanStack Query/Table); its build output is what `/ui` serves.
The layout is the Workbench mockup: header with Search · Browse · Map · Runs · Fact-check tabs, three panes (filters | results | detail), and a status footer.
Dark theme is the default and uses the TUI theme colors (#18181B background, #A78BFA accent, #7DD3FC secondary); a light theme toggle exists and the choice persists.
Switching theme flips instantly with no color cross-fade.
The footer shows live status for Postgres, the Ollama embedder, and any running ingest or fact-check job.
Search runs hybrid RRF and every result shows its keyword rank, vector rank, and fused score.
A mode toggle switches search between Keyword, Vector, and Hybrid RRF.
Query terms are highlighted in result text.
If the embedder is down, hybrid search still returns keyword results and shows a 'vector leg unavailable' warning.
Concurrent searches from the server never call `dspy.configure()` / `setup_dspy_router()` inside a worker thread.
The Browse tab lists all clauses in a virtualized table that scrolls smoothly through the full corpus (5,991+ rows).
Browse filters cover notebook, document, run, strategy, fact-check status, length range, and quality flag, each value showing its count.
A quality detector flags noise chunks — base64/binary blobs and numeric-table rows — and the Quality filter shows their counts.
Selecting a chunk opens the detail pane with its parent chunk text and the clause highlighted inside it.
'More like this' lists nearest-neighbor chunks by embedding distance with the distance value, and marks near-duplicates (distance under a set threshold) with a 'near-duplicate' badge.
'More like this' lists nearest-neighbor chunks by embedding distance, showing the distance value.
Delete works at four levels: a clause, a parent chunk with its children, a whole document, or a whole run.
A committed delete removes the rows plus their embeddings and fact_checks, and writes one `removal_log` row per delete action.
Delete opens a confirmation dialog that names the level and counts (clauses, embeddings, fact-checks) to be removed; nothing is deleted until confirmed, and Cancel removes nothing.
Multi-select (checkbox, `x` key, shift-click range) opens a bulk bar with Delete, Export, and Re-fact-check.
Export downloads the selected chunks as Markdown or JSON.
Export can push the selected chunks as a note into their source NotebookLM notebook.
'Ask' sends the question plus top retrieved chunks to NotebookLM `chat.ask`, scoped to those chunks' source IDs, with chunks labeled [C1]…[Cn] in the prompt.
Answers show inline [Cn] citations; clicking one opens that chunk in the detail pane.
A model picker accepts any litellm model string; answers from a picked model stream token by token over SSE.
While NotebookLM is answering (non-streaming), the UI shows a progress state.
The Map tab shows a 2D projection of chunk embeddings, colored by document (by topic once topics exist); clicking a point opens that chunk.
The Runs tab lists chunk_runs with strategy, parent/child counts, mean and p95 length, and active flag.
While ingestion runs, counts refresh every 5 seconds and a 'N new chunks' pill appears; clicking it refreshes the results.
The Fact-check tab starts a run for a notebook, or for selected chunks via Re-fact-check.
The run queue lists every chunk with its status (pending, active, verified, refuted, skipped, waiting) plus progress counts and elapsed time.
When the satire/meta-dialogue classifier flags a chunk, the run pauses and the UI shows the gate with the classifier probability and Skip (Y), Fact-check (N), Auto-skip toggle (S).
The active chunk is shown with the 2 transcript lines before and after it.
The evidence log shows verdict, confidence, rationale, and a Langfuse trace link per chunk; the active chunk shows SIFT step status.
Run events reach the browser over SSE; closing the tab does not stop the run, and reopening shows its current state.
The fact-check gate logic lives in `_app/`; the TUI Fact-check mode uses the same code and keeps its y/n/s behavior.
Cmd/Ctrl-K opens a command palette that can switch tabs, focus search, delete the selection, start a fact-check run, and toggle theme.
Keyboard shortcuts: `/` focus search, `j`/`k` move, `x` select, `Enter` open, `Backspace` delete, `?` shortcut sheet.
The TUI SFL panel shows Tenor, Mood, and Modality values (not field names) when the SFL result is a nested dict; TUI and web use one shared SFL formatter.
Buttons scale to 0.96 on press, and no stylesheet uses `transition: all`.
pytest covers every `/v1/corpus` route against the real Postgres, and those tests fail (not skip) when Postgres is unreachable.
Vitest component tests pass for search results, detail pane, undo toast, fact-check gate, and command palette.
A Playwright smoke test passes: search → open chunk → delete → Cancel (row still present) → delete → Confirm (row gone).
ruff, mypy, and the existing pytest suite (90% coverage gate) still pass.
SFL tagging can be started for any corpus document, run, or chunk selection (from Browse, Runs, or Fact-check), not only for a whole notebook.
A fact-check run, gate included, can target any document, run, or chunk selection: sources, notes, and ingested artifacts alike.
An 'Ingest artifact' action lists a notebook's NotebookLM artifacts and adds the chosen one to the corpus as its own document, keyed by artifact ID.

Audio and video artifacts are converted to a temporary FLAC (mono, original sample rate, 16-bit or 24-bit for 24-bit sources, 80 Hz high-pass, −19 LUFS with peaks capped at −1 dBFS), sent to the chosen provider, and the temp file is deleted afterward; speaker labels stay in the chunk text and the original audio is never modified.
Report, quiz, flashcard, mind map, and data table artifacts are converted to text (Markdown, outline, or rows) and ingested without transcription.

Infographic and slide-deck artifacts appear in the list but are disabled ('image-only, not ingestible yet'); artifact conversion goes through a per-kind converter registry so image/audio/video embedding (e.g. a multimodal Gemma embedder) can be added later without changing callers.
Every corpus document shows its kind (source, note, audio, video, report, quiz, flashcards, mind map, data table), and Browse can filter by kind.

Ingesting an artifact whose content checksum matches an existing run's `source_hash` is skipped ('already ingested, unchanged'); it is re-ingested only when the checksum differs or the user picks 'Force re-ingest', and then the new run replaces the old one as active.

The audio/video ingest dialog matches the audio-segment-extractor panel: provider choice (Speechmatics, AssemblyAI, Deepgram, local transcribe_cpp), a 'key found / key missing' line for the chosen provider, a Diarize toggle, a Language selector defaulting to Auto-detect, and a Transcribe button.
facts.comment: add these as config or .env key/vals fr setting defaults

facts.text: Clause fact-check runs can use the Jev decision model as the check-worthiness gate (choices: checkworthy, meta-dialogue/satire, filler); the gate card shows Jev's probability for the chosen label.
The rule-based `checkworthiness.assess` gate stays selectable, and a comparison script reports agreement between the Jev gate and the rule gate on a sample of stored chunks.

When retrieved chunks span more than one notebook, Ask runs a DSPy corpus pipeline: a `dspy.ReAct` agent with tools (corpus search, chunk detail, neighbors, NotebookLM ask for one notebook), and `dspy.MultiChainComparison` merges the per-notebook answers into one answer with [Cn] citations.
An experimental 'Deep' Ask mode uses `dspy.RLM` to explore contexts too large for one prompt; it is labeled experimental in the UI and shows a clear error if its sandbox is unavailable.
Browse can filter to chunks that have at least one near-duplicate.
DSPy work in the server binds the LM with `dspy.context(lm=...)` in workers; `dspy.configure()` is only called once, on the main thread at server startup.
